{"path":"/work/tests/test_priority.py","content":"import json

import pytest

from todo.api import create_task, list_tasks, update_task
from todo.store import Store


def test_default_priority(tmp_path):
    s = Store(str(tmp_path / "s.json"))
    t = create_task(s, {"title": "a"})
    assert t["priority"] == "normal"


def test_create_with_priority(tmp_path):
    s = Store(str(tmp_path / "s.json"))
    t = create_task(s, {"title": "a", "priority": "high"})
    assert t["priority"] == "high"


def test_create_unknown_priority_not_saved(tmp_path):
    p = str(tmp_path / "s.json")
    s = Store(p)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        create_task(s, {"title": "a", "priority": "urgent"})
    assert s.tasks == {}
    assert not list_tasks(s)
    # nothing was written to disk by the failed create
    s2 = Store(p)
    assert s2.tasks == {}


def test_update_priority(tmp_path):
    s = Store(str(tmp_path / "s.json"))
    t = create_task(s, {"title": "a"})
    assert update_task(s, t["id"], {"priority": "low"})["priority"] == "low"
    assert update_task(s, t["id"], {"priority": "high"})["priority"] == "high"


def test_update_unknown_priority_rejected(tmp_path):
    s = Store(str(tmp_path / "s.json"))
    t = create_task(s, {"title": "a"})
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        update_task(s, t["id"], {"priority": "bogus"})
    assert s.tasks[t["id"]].priority == "normal"


def test_priority_roundtrip(tmp_path):
    p = str(tmp_path / "s.json")
    s = Store(p)
    create_task(s, {"title": "a", "priority": "high"})
    create_task(s, {"title": "b"})
    s2 = Store(p)
    tasks = list_tasks(s2)
    assert [t["priority"] for t in tasks] == ["high", "normal"]
    on_disk = json.load(open(p))["tasks"]
    assert on_disk[0]["priority"] == "high"
    assert on_disk[1]["priority"] == "normal"


def test_old_store_without_priority_loads(tmp_path):
    p = str(tmp_path / "s.json")
    with open(p, "w") as f:
        json.dump({"version": 1, "tasks": [{"id": 1, "title": "a", "done": True}]}, f)
    s = Store(p)
    tasks = list_tasks(s)
    assert [t["priority"] for t in tasks] == ["normal"]


def test_list_filter_by_priority(tmp_path):
    s = Store(str(tmp_path / "s.json"))
    create_task(s, {"title": "a", "priority": "high"})
    create_task(s, {"title": "b"})
    create_task(s, {"title": "c", "priority": "low"})
    assert [t["title"] for t in list_tasks(s, priority="high")] == ["a"]
    assert [t["title"] for t in list_tasks(s, priority="normal")] == ["b"]
    assert [t["title"] for t in list_tasks(s, priority="low")] == ["c"]
    assert list_tasks(s, priority="high", done=True) == []


def test_list_sort_by_priority(tmp_path):
    s = Store(str(tmp_path / "s.json"))
    create_task(s, {"title": "a"})          # id 1 normal
    create_task(s, {"title": "b", "priority": "low"})   # id 2 low
    create_task(s, {"title": "c", "priority": "high"})  # id 3 high
    create_task(s, {"title": "d"})          # id 4 normal
    create_task(s, {"title": "e", "priority": "high"})  # id 5 high
    create_task(s, {"title": "f", "priority": "low"})   # id 6 low
    ts = list_tasks(s, sort="priority")
    assert [t["title"] for t in ts] == ["c", "e", "a", "d", "b", "f"]
    # default order unchanged: by id
    assert [t["title"] for t in list_tasks(s)] == ["a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"]


def test_every_dict_includes_priority(tmp_path):
    s = Store(str(tmp_path / "s.json"))
    t = create_task(s, {"title": "a"})
    assert set(t) == {"id", "title", "done", "priority"}
    assert all("priority" in x for x in list_tasks(s))

All 13 tests pass (3 original + 10 new).

Summary of changes:
- `todo/model.py` — `Task` gains `priority: str = "normal"`; `validate()` rejects values outside `("low", "normal", "high")`. Added `PRIORITIES` / `DEFAULT_PRIORITY` constants.
- `todo/store.py` — saves `"priority"` per task and loads it with `d.get("priority", DEFAULT_PRIORITY)`, so pre-existing stores without the field load as "normal".
- `todo/serialize.py` — `task_to_dict` now includes `"priority"` in every returned task dict.
- `todo/api.py` — `create_task` accepts an optional `priority` (validated via `_priority_from_payload`, raises `ValueError` before anything is saved or written); `update_task` handles `"priority"` in the payload with the same validation (rejected updates leave the task unchanged); `list_tasks` gains `priority=` filtering and `sort="priority"` ordering (high → normal → low, stable by id), with default order unchanged.
- `tests/test_priority.py` — new tests covering defaults, validation on create/update (nothing saved/rejected values kept), JSON round-trip, legacy store loading, filtering, sorting, and that every dict includes `priority`.
